body: I'm pretty sure I ran into this once, but my issue was on main with updated wgpu and winit. It happened once and hasn't happened again, if I manage to reproduce it I will try to add some details here or create a new issue.

`2023-12-31T00:14:46.257796Z ERROR log: X11 error: XError {
    description: "BadWindow (invalid Window parameter)",
    error_code: 3,
    request_code: 148,
    minor_code: 1,
}`

just hit it again on up to date main, confirmed to be the same error as above, in my case it's during a normally clean shutdown where I'm sending an exit event after transitioning to my `Game::Exit` `AppState`.

I'm on Pop!_OS 22.04 (6.5.6-76060506-generic) and I wasn't able to reproduce this. I tried your code with and without tiling enabled, and opened and closed ~50 windows a few times. Here's the error location in `winit` ([link](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/2ebbfab6a47f93f76841553dcb3cc53683e4955c/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs#L936)) and the method that returns the result ([link](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/c55a2c779b5521c24121515fbc969718fb704cd3/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/ime/mod.rs#L196)). Did some digging and looks like this is the relevant X11 doc: [link](https://www.x.org/releases/current/doc/libX11/libX11/libX11.html#Input_Focus_Events). Can you get the error with a backtrace? That might be helpful.

I did some digging in the meantime with a standalone `winit` program to see if I could recreate the issue that way in order to single out `winit` as a cause. I haven't been able to reproduce the issue with the most barebones program I could set up (see below). 
I will admit however that `bevy_winit` and advanced `winit` usage go a little over my head, so if somebody else has a more sophisticated (potentially closer to Bevy's use) idea for a test program, I'd be more than happy to test that and report my findings.
<details>
    <summary>winit app used for testing</summary>

Using `winit`  0.28.7 (same version as Bevy 0.12.1).
I opened around 100 windows in 4 different test runs and haven't encountered the crash once, while the average windows I need to close with Bevy in order to crash seems to be just below 10.

```rs
use std::collections::HashMap;
use winit::{window::{WindowBuilder, WindowId, Window}, dpi::LogicalSize, event_loop::{EventLoopWindowTarget, EventLoop}, event::{Event, WindowEvent, ElementState, KeyboardInput}};

static mut WINDOWS: i32 = 1;

fn spawn_window<T>(wt: &EventLoopWindowTarget<T>, windows: &mut HashMap<WindowId, Window>) {
    let window_no = unsafe { WINDOWS };
    
    let builder = WindowBuilder::new()
        .with_title(format!("{}", window_no))
        .with_inner_size(LogicalSize::new(1280.0_f32, 720.0_f32))
        .with_visible(true);

    println!("Opening window #{window_no}.");

    unsafe {
        WINDOWS += 1;
    }

    let window = builder.build(wt).unwrap();
    let id = window.id();

    windows.insert(id, window);
}

fn main() {
    let mut windows = HashMap::new();
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new();
    
    spawn_window(&event_loop, &mut windows);

    event_loop.run(move |event: Event<()>, elwt, flow| {
        if let Event::WindowEvent { window_id, event } = event {
            match event {
                WindowEvent::CloseRequested => {
                    println!("Closing window with ID {window_id:?}");

                    // drop the window here
                    windows.remove(&window_id);

                    if windows.is_empty() {
                        flow.set_exit();
                    }
                },
                WindowEvent::KeyboardInput { input: KeyboardInput { scancode, state: ElementState::Released, .. }, .. } => {
                    // space scancode on my machine; may need to adjust
                    if scancode == 57 {
                        println!("Spawning window.");
                        spawn_window(elwt, &mut windows);
                    }
                },
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    });
}
```
</details>

I also did some patching on `winit` (albeit naive, since I'm not familiar enough with its or X11's inner workings) and found that if I prevent the crash in the [`ffi::XI_FocusIn` handler](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/c55a2c779b5521c24121515fbc969718fb704cd3/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs#L968) by returning early if the window doesn't exist (exact same logic as in [`ffi::XI_FocusOut` handler](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/c55a2c779b5521c24121515fbc969718fb704cd3/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs#L968); reasoning being a comment I saw in `ffi:XI_Leave` [here](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/c55a2c779b5521c24121515fbc969718fb704cd3/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs#L956C43-L956C43)), I get a different crash in the later [`ffi::DestroyNotify` handler](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/blob/c55a2c779b5521c24121515fbc969718fb704cd3/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs#L968) at `remove_context`. But that feels a little too deep into `winit` internals to be a problem with Bevy.

I've found a way to reproduce this now it seems, a sequence of rapid inputs to bevy_ui seems to cause it to trigger reliably, no closer on a MRE. I think maybe a ui pressed event is being processed at the same time `AppExit` event is destroying the window. There is no crash, so I haven't gotten much more info, entering my game client and rapidly clicking buttons a few times and clicking exit gets me the error message. It seems to be masked by schedule build order changing between runs of my client to further complicate this. There could be some ordering constraint missing in bevy, or it's rooted deeper, perhaps in winit.

issue.body:
* Bevy version: 425570aa752b32ef26f6573b385d49d6254bd868 (main as of today)
* Linux/X11

## What you did

* Run the `multiple_windows` example with `cargo run --example multiple_windows`.

## What went wrong

Closing a window results in a panic with the following error:
```
bevy_winit: winit event loop returned an error: os error at
cargo/registry/src/winit-0.29.9/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/mod.rs:433:
Xlib error: X error: BadWindow (invalid Window parameter) (code: 3, request code: 148, minor code: 1)
```

## Additional information

Probably related to #10702

issue.body:
# Objective

Fixes #11236
~~(likely)~~ Fixes #11150 
~~(likely)~~ Fixes #11734

## Problem

Window crashes when using pipelined rendering under GPU-bound scenarios.

It is not exclusive to XWayland and is based on a race condition with pipelined rendering. 

Winit windows might be deleted on app world while the window is still alive in render world, if the render world window tries to access a winit resource (i.e. a surface or raw handle) it panics because the winit window no longer exists.
All those crashes go away by disabling pipelined rendering.

## Solution

- `Arc<WinitWindow>` and extract it when using pipelined rendering.

## Alternative solutions

- Delay deleting WinitWindow by a frame.

issue.body:
# Objective

A `RawWindowHandle` is only valid as long as the window it was retrieved from is alive. Extend the lifetime of the window, so that the `RawWindowHandle` doesn't outlive it, and bevy doesn't crash when closing a window a pipelined renderer is drawing to.

- Fix #11236
- Fix #11150
- Fix #11734
- Alternative to / Closes #12524

## Solution

Introduce a `WindowWrapper` that takes ownership of the window. Require it to be used when constructing a `RawHandleWrapper`. This forces windowing backends to store their window in this wrapper.

The `WindowWrapper` is implemented by storing the window in an `Arc<dyn Any + Send + Sync>`.

We use dynamic dispatch here because we later want the `RawHandleWrapper` to be able dynamically hold a reference to any windowing backend's window.

But alas, the `WindowWrapper` itself is still practically invisible to windowing backends, because it implements `Deref` to the underlying window, by storing its type in a `PhantomData`.

---

## Changelog

### Added

- Added `WindowWrapper`, which windowing backends are now required to use to store their underlying window.

### Fixed

- Fixed a safety problem which caused crashes when closing bevy windows when using pipelined rendering.

## Migration Guide

- Windowing backends now need to store their window in the new `WindowWrapper`.
